findings.summary: Part 2 opens with the override merge-rule table before ever stating that override files exist or how they are loaded, so the rules precede the mechanism they govern.
findings.evidence: Page 1's first block is `{"type":"heading","text":"Merge Rules By Type"}` followed by the table rows `["scalar","`image`, `command`","replaced"]` … while the fact that merging happens at all only appears on page 2: "`up` auto-loads `compose.yaml` ==and== `compose.override.yaml`" and "Later files override earlier ones — ==order matters==".
findings.fix: Move page 2's "Which Files Load" and "Explicit -f Chains" sections to the top of page 1, ahead of "Merge Rules By Type", so the learner knows what two files are being merged before reading how they merge.

findings.summary: The "The Real Answer" callout on page 2 says "Neither" in reference to two options that are not introduced until page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 callout: "The Real Answer — Neither. Put nginx, Traefik or Caddy in front and let it resolve the service name — DNS hands it every replica IP." The two options it rejects appear on page 3: "Publish a range: `\"8080-8082:80\"`" and "Or omit the host port — `\"80\"` gets ephemeral ports". Page 2's surrounding content is about replica counts, not host ports, so "Neither" has no antecedent.
findings.fix: Move this callout to page 3, directly after the "Two ways out" bullets under "The Fixed-Port Wall", where the two rejected options have just been stated.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a boilerplate series label with no hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER COMPOSE: THE MULTI-CONTAINER HANDBOOK. `depends_on` does not mean ready — it means started, and that one misreading has crashed more stacks than any Dockerfile bug."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the series label after it: "`depends_on` does not mean ready — it means started, and that one misreading has crashed more stacks than any Dockerfile bug. Part 2 of DOCKER COMPOSE: THE MULTI-CONTAINER HANDBOOK."

findings.summary: The override-files topic is cut in half by scaling content, so the learner is moved off overrides and back onto them across three pages.
findings.evidence: Page 1 ends with "Scaling, Two Ways" and `docker compose up -d --scale worker=5`; page 2 opens with "`deploy.replicas` is honored by V2 without Swarm" and "Where The Count Comes From", then reverses to "Which Files Load" / "Explicit -f Chains"; page 3 returns to scaling with "The Fixed-Port Wall".
findings.fix: Keep all override material (merge rules, path/reuse gotchas, canonical layout, which files load, -f chains, verify-with-config) contiguous, and start scaling only once — move the page 1 "Scaling, Two Ways" block to the head of the scaling run that begins page 3.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: Page 7 opens with an override-merge callout six pages after the override section closed, and it contradicts the classification page 1 gave for the same keys.
findings.evidence: Page 7 callout: "Lists Append — Override files do not replace `ports`, `volumes` or `dns`." Page 1's table classifies those keys differently: `["sequence","`dns`, `expose`, `tmpfs`","appended"]` and `["unique","`ports`, `volumes`, `secrets`","merged by key"]`.
findings.fix: Move this callout back into the page 1 "Appending Is The Trap" section and reword it to match the table — dns/expose/tmpfs append, while ports/volumes merge on their unique key so a differing published port or target path leaves both entries in place.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The one-line recap of the four areas is split across pages 8 and 9, with page 9 restating the same four areas in a different form before its own titled topic.
findings.evidence: Page 8's table gives "Network / Volumes / Env / Overrides" one-liners ("Overrides","scalars replace, maps merge, lists append"); page 9 then opens, before any heading, with "Publish ports only for host access, nothing else", "`-v` on `down` is a loaded gun", "Secrets belong in files, not variables", "Base + `compose.override.yaml` for dev, `-f prod` for prod" — the same four areas again.
findings.fix: Fold page 9's opening four bullets and the "Scaling In One Line" callout into page 8's one-liner section so each area is summarised once, and let page 9 begin with the debug loop its title promises.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: `extends:` and `include:` are introduced as reuse mechanisms with no syntax example, unlike the neighbouring `!override`/`!reset` which get one.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "`extends:` pulls in one service definition from elsewhere", "`include:` (2.20+) composes whole sub-files into one project" — no code block follows, while the preceding trap does get one: `ports: !override ["80:80"]  # replace list`.
findings.fix: Add a two-line YAML example under the section, e.g. `extends: {file: common.yaml, service: base}` and `include: ["./db/compose.yaml"]`, so the keys are usable from the page.

findings.summary: The pushpin graphic on the yellow "one host port per replica" callout sits on top of the code line above it, partly covering a word.
findings.evidence: Code line `ports: ["80"]  # ephemeral host` — the red pin icon overlaps the final word "host" in the comment.
findings.fix: Offset the pinned callout downward (or reduce its pin's negative top offset) so the pin anchors below the last code line instead of on top of it.

findings.summary: Page 3, titled for scaling limits, ends with two tool-comparison sections that belong to the following chapter.
findings.evidence: Page 3 is titled "Scaling Limits: Ports, State & Shutdown" yet closes with "Against docker run" ("Same API calls, but persisted, versioned and reviewable") and "Against The Dockerfile" ("Dockerfile builds one image — build time").
findings.fix: Move both sections to the head of page 4 ("Compose vs Swarm vs Kubernetes") so the comparison chapter starts on its own page instead of trailing the scaling chapter.

findings.summary: Page 10 opens with extra `docker compose config` flags, orphaned from the debug-loop section on page 9 where `config` is taught.
findings.evidence: Page 10's first block, with no heading above it: "`config --no-interpolate` keeps `${VAR}` unexpanded", "`config --resolve-image-digests` pins tags to digests", "Invalid YAML makes `config` exit non-zero — a **CI lint**". Page 9 is where `config` is introduced: "`config`: what will run · `ps`: what is running" and the "Debug Commands" block showing `docker compose config --services`.
findings.fix: Move these three bullets under page 9's "Debug Commands" heading so all `config` variants are taught together, leaving page 10 to start with the production checklist.
